quotes.text: Azure lighthouse lets one organization manage another organization's Azure resources from its own environment without needing an account inside the other organizations directory.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: One-sentence definition of what Azure Lighthouse does.

quotes.text: What makes this different from simply handing somebody your password is that the door is written down. It has a name, a scope, and a role attached to it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why delegation is safer than shared credentials.

quotes.text: That means access isn't a one time handshake you hope was done correctly. It's checked on every action over and over for as long as the door exists.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies that delegated access is verified on every request.

quotes.text: The biggest confusion to clear up is that lighthouse is a management tool rather than a data tool.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets a clear boundary on what Lighthouse can and cannot reach.

quotes.text: If a customer places a lock on their resources to stop things from being changed or deleted, that lock doesn't stop a provider's users from acting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Flags a security gap that surprises many customers.

takeaways: Azure Lighthouse lets a provider manage a customer's Azure resources from its own tenant through a registration definition and a registration assignment, with no account in the customer's directory.
The customer chooses the scope and built-in role, sees every provider action in its own activity log and can remove the delegation at any time.
Lighthouse covers Azure Resource Manager operations only, does not support the Owner role or data-access roles, and is a different product from Microsoft 365 Lighthouse.
hook: Managed service providers and multi-tenant enterprises have long juggled separate logins in every customer tenant. This episode explains how Azure Lighthouse replaces that with delegated, auditable access that the customer controls, and where its limits are. You will be able to explain the handshake, the security model and the naming trap with Microsoft 365 Lighthouse.
